text.p: UK equity options were thinly traded on Tuesday, reflecting the slow motion in underlying stocks, dealers said.
The big trade in conglomerate Hanson was a short straddle from a trader selling 1,000 November 160 puts at 7p as well as 1,000 November 160 calls also at 7p.
The deal stands to make a maximum profit of 14p if the underlying shares are 160p at expiry.
Over in Prudential Corporation news that the insurer had sold its Mercantile & General reinsurance business today may have prompted the purchase of 500 November 460 calls at 11p.
The M&G business was sold to Swiss Re for 1.75 billion stg ($2.73 billion). Funds raised from the sale are expected to give Prudential scope for further expansion in other areas of finacial services.
The main deal in pay-television broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting was from a seller of 200 March 500 puts at 8-1/2p.

If the underlying shares stay above 500p by March expiry, the 8-1/2p premium will be the maximum profit from the deal. Traders said stock shortage helped lift the underlying shares despite them going ex-dividend today by 3p net of basic tax.
At 1400 GMT, BSkyB shares were up 9-1/2p to 587-1/2p while shares in Prudential added 1-1/2p to 438-1/2p. Hanson shares gained 1-3/4p to 161-1/4p.
